title: Umm Habibah
hook: Abu Sufyan's daughter, who believed while her father opposed the Prophet, and emigrated to Abyssinia

segments.voice: Yesterday: Juwayriyyah, who walked in to ask, and whose people walked out free. Your line was a blessing to her people.

Her father would come to lead the Quraysh against the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. That father was Abu Sufyan, and his daughter Ramlah, known as Umm Habibah, had become a Muslim anyway. She left Mecca with the emigrants across the sea to Abyssinia, far from her family. Years of opposition between her house and her faith. And then one day, in Ibn Ishaq's telling, her father walks into her room in Medina. Today: Umm Habibah.
screen: `HER FATHER LEADS THE OPPOSITION.` → `SHE BELIEVES ANYWAY.` → `HER FATHER WALKS IN.`

segments.voice: Start in Abyssinia. Umm Habibah went there as an emigrant with her first husband, and her first marriage ended there, far from home. Sunan Abi Dawud preserves what happened next: the marriage between her and the Prophet was arranged in Abyssinia, with the Negus, the Christian king who had sheltered the Muslims, giving the dowry on the Prophet's behalf. The daughter of a leader of the opposition, married to him in a Christian king's land. Now the visit. Ibn Ishaq says Abu Sufyan came to Medina, still not a Muslim, trying to shore up a treaty his side had broken. He went to his daughter's room and was about to sit on the Prophet's bedding. She folded it away. He asked whether she thought the bedding too good for him, or him too good for it. She answered that it was the Messenger's place, and he was still a man who worshipped idols. Strong words to a father. The sirah keeps them as a picture of faith set above a family's pride. But hold a second report beside it, this one in Bukhari. Years later, when news reached her of Abu Sufyan's death, Umm Habibah, on the third day, called for perfume and put it on. She said she had no need of perfume, but she had heard the Prophet say a believing woman should not mourn more than three days, except for a husband. She did mourn her father. She just kept her mourning within what she had been taught. Faith before family pride did not mean faith without family love. It meant knowing which came first.
screen: `A MARRIAGE MADE IN ABYSSINIA.` · `SHE FOLDS AWAY THE BEDDING.` · `IT IS THE MESSENGER'S PLACE.` · `SHE MOURNS HER FATHER THREE DAYS.` · then, large: `FAITH BEFORE FAMILY PRIDE.`

segments.voice: Think of a place, if there is one, where what you hold most deeply and what your family expects don't line up, about faith or anything else you care about. Breathe in and name what you won't let go of; breathe out and name one thing you love about that family member anyway. If you pray, pray for them by name.
Umm Habibah. Abu Sufyan's daughter, who believed while her father opposed the Prophet, married the Prophet in Abyssinia, and still mourned her father when he died. Today's word.
Your line: faith before family pride. Faith first, and still never faith without love. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Umm Habibah, Ramlah bint Abi Sufyan, among the mothers of the believers and among the emigrants to Abyssinia; her rule of mourning from Sahih al-Bukhari is part of how Muslims learn the limits of mourning.

fork.setup: your father, who still opposes the Prophet, comes into your room and is about to sit on the Prophet's bedding. what do you do?
options: let him sit; he's your father.
fork.reveal: in Ibn Ishaq she folds it away and tells him it is the Messenger's place. Bukhari later shows her mourning him when he dies.

original.note: Arabic: 'mother of Habibah', after her daughter; her own name was Ramlah.

trapdoor: what you thought: a daughter who simply cut off her family.
what it means: she set faith above her family's pride, and still mourned her father.
what a scholar hears: Ibn Ishaq for the folded bedding; Sunan Abi Dawud 2107 for the marriage in Abyssinia; Bukhari 1280 for the three days of mourning and the perfume.
recall: whose house was declared a sanctuary

chat.says: Did Umm Habibah stop loving her father because he opposed the Prophet?
options: No. She put faith first, yet still mourned him when he died.
Yes. She cut him off and never spoke of him again.
No. She hid her faith from him to keep the peace at home.
chat.meaning: She folded away the bedding, yet in Bukhari she mourned Abu Sufyan three days. Faith before family pride did not mean faith without family love.

Umm Habibah.meaning: a mother of the believers; her own name was Ramlah

notes: Hadith numbers cited from memory; confirm.
Her first husband, Ubaydullah ibn Jahsh, is left unnamed, and the sirah's report of his leaving Islam is left out; the script says only that her first marriage ended there. Confirm framing.
The bedding story is from Ibn Ishaq; confirm wording and that it is presented as sirah rather than hadith.
'Years later' for Abu Sufyan's death is vague on purpose; no date given under the claims rule. 'Years of opposition' in the hook is also unnumbered; Keeper may soften.
'Her own name was Ramlah' and 'after her daughter Habibah': confirm.
